project.name: mobile-automator
project.description: Host-agnostic mauto CLI for AI-driven mobile QA automation — analyzes a mobile project and drives devices through mobile-mcp. Note: this project has over 100 source files; consider scoping analysis to a subdirectory for faster results.

nodes.name: mauto-session-daemon.js
nodes.summary: Entry point for the persistent mobile-mcp session daemon process; parses CLI flags, wires up the daemon with a recorder and flusher, and cleans up workspace artifacts on exit.

nodes.name: cleanupWorkspaceIfOwned
nodes.summary: Removes the daemon's socket, pid, lock, and handle files from the workspace when the recorded pid still belongs to this process.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Parses daemon flags and starts the persistent session daemon with a recorder and flusher, installing fatal-error and signal handlers.

nodes.name: device-call.js
nodes.summary: Wraps a single mobile-mcp tool call with session wiring, per-call id, timeout, and observation events so device verbs get uniform telemetry.

nodes.name: makeDeviceCall
nodes.summary: Builds and executes one mobile-mcp tool call, enforcing a timeout, recording success/failure observation events, and returning the normalized tool result.

nodes.name: mobile-mcp-tools.js
nodes.summary: Defines the fixed set of mobile-mcp tool names the CLI is allowed to call, with a predicate for validating tool names at runtime.

nodes.name: isKnownTool
nodes.summary: Returns whether a tool name is in the allowed mobile-mcp tool set.

nodes.name: session-daemon.js
nodes.summary: Implements the persistent session daemon: acquires workspace locks, serves framed requests over a Unix socket, arms idle/flush timers, and stops cleanly.

nodes.name: pidAlive
nodes.summary: Checks whether a pid is a live process via a zero-signal kill probe.

nodes.name: pidIdentity
nodes.summary: Verifies a pid belongs to a mauto-session-daemon process by inspecting its command line.

nodes.name: cleanStale
nodes.summary: Removes leftover socket, pid, lock, and handle files from a dead daemon so the workspace can be re-acquired.

nodes.name: startDaemon
nodes.summary: Boots the full daemon: locks the workspace, creates the Unix socket server, handles framed requests, and manages idle/shutdown lifecycle.

nodes.name: accepts.js
nodes.summary: Provides sendability predicates and catalog validation helpers used to decide which event fields are allowed on the wire for telemetry.

nodes.name: oneOf
nodes.summary: Returns a predicate tagging values that belong to a fixed set.

nodes.name: matches
nodes.summary: Returns a predicate tagging values that match a regular expression.

nodes.name: integer
nodes.summary: Predicate tagging integer values as sendable.

nodes.name: boolean
nodes.summary: Predicate tagging boolean values as sendable.

nodes.name: isoTimestamp
nodes.summary: Predicate tagging valid ISO timestamp strings as sendable.

nodes.name: sendable
nodes.summary: Predicate deciding whether a field basis is allowed for sending.

nodes.name: findUnenforced
nodes.summary: Finds catalog entries marked sends:true whose accepts basis disagrees with their declared basis.

nodes.name: event.js
nodes.summary: Defines the observation event shape: the EVENT_FIELDS catalog, ambient fields, makeEvent constructor, and telemetry payload projection.

nodes.name: makeEvent
nodes.summary: Constructs a normalized observation event with timestamp, session id, and catalog-enforced fields.

nodes.name: telemetryPayload
nodes.summary: Projects an event onto the subset of fields approved for telemetry sending.

nodes.name: failure-capture.js
nodes.summary: Captures failure evidence — a device screenshot and trace events — when a run fails, and records the capture outcome.

nodes.name: isCapturable
nodes.summary: Decides whether a failure kind warrants screenshot capture.

nodes.name: failureShotPath
nodes.summary: Builds the filesystem path for a failure screenshot using a safe verb token.

nodes.name: captureOnFailure
nodes.summary: Takes a device screenshot on failure, writes it into the workspace, and records capture events to the run trace.

nodes.name: flush.js
nodes.summary: Periodic telemetry flusher that claims spooled batches, chunks them, posts them via transport, and prunes claimed files on success.

nodes.name: makeFlusher
nodes.summary: Creates a flusher that drains the spool in bounded batches, posts them to the telemetry endpoint, and cleans up on success or over-quota.

nodes.name: paths.js
nodes.summary: Central path resolution for the observe subsystem: workspace, logs, daemon event log, spool, and run-trace file locations.

nodes.name: workspaceDir
nodes.summary: Returns the project workspace root.

nodes.name: logsDir
nodes.summary: Returns the logs directory under the workspace.

nodes.name: mainLogPath
nodes.summary: Path to the main CLI log file.

nodes.name: daemonEventLogPath
nodes.summary: Path to the daemon's NDJSON event log.

nodes.name: spoolPath

nodes.name: isValidRunId
nodes.summary: Validates a run-id directory name against the run-id pattern.

nodes.name: runTracePath
nodes.summary: Path to a run's trace NDJSON file.

nodes.name: recorder.js
nodes.summary: Recorder facade that builds default sinks (stderr, file, spool), normalizes events, and exposes a safe observe wrapper for daemon use.

nodes.name: defaultSinks
nodes.summary: Builds the default stderr, file, and spool sinks honoring env log levels and telemetry decisions.

nodes.name: record
nodes.summary: Constructs an observation event and writes it to every active sink.

nodes.name: safeObserve
nodes.summary: Calls observe() inside a try/catch so daemon paths cannot be crashed by a throwing observer.

nodes.name: boundRecorder
nodes.summary: Binds record to a fixed workspace and env with default sinks for use inside the daemon.

nodes.name: settings.js
nodes.summary: Resolves observation log levels from the environment and normalizes the run id used by the recorder.

nodes.name: resolveLevels
nodes.summary: Resolves stderr and file log levels from MAUTO_LOG_LEVEL with defaults.

nodes.name: atLeast
nodes.summary: Returns true when the resolved log level meets a minimum threshold.

nodes.name: resolveRunId

nodes.name: spool.js

nodes.name: newMessageId
nodes.summary: Generates a random spool message id.

nodes.name: write

nodes.name: claim
nodes.summary: Renames the spool to a claimed batch file stamped with the claim time.

nodes.name: listClaimed
nodes.summary: Lists claimed batch files sorted by claim stamp.

nodes.name: readBatch
nodes.summary: Parses a claimed batch file back into event objects.

nodes.name: stats
nodes.summary: Reports spool byte size and pending batch counts.

nodes.name: envKillSwitch
nodes.summary: Returns whether the DO_NOT_TRACK environment variable disables telemetry for this process.

nodes.name: resolveTelemetry
nodes.summary: Resolves the telemetry enabled state from environment and token presence.

nodes.name: decideForProject
nodes.summary: Memoized per-project telemetry decision computed from config and environment.

nodes.name: setEnabled
nodes.summary: Persists the telemetry preference through the config manager.

nodes.name: _resetMemo

nodes.name: sentFields

nodes.name: neverSentFields
nodes.summary: Lists event fields never sent to telemetry.

nodes.name: resolveToken

nodes.name: hasToken

nodes.summary: Posts a batch of wire events to the telemetry endpoint with token and deadline.

nodes.name: splitList
nodes.summary: Splits a raw comma-separated string into trimmed non-empty parts.

nodes.name: coerceValue
nodes.summary: Coerces a raw CLI string into the declared type for a dotted config key: JSON parsing for arrays/objects, string passthrough, null handling, and a lenient pass-through for undeclared keys.

nodes.name: normalizeConfig
nodes.summary: Heals every declared list path in a config object that holds a string, splitting it into an array; leaves everything else exactly as found.

nodes.name: configDir
nodes.summary: Returns the mobile-automator directory path under a project root.

nodes.name: configPath
nodes.summary: Returns the config.json path under a project root.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Reads and parses config.json, returning null when absent and healing pre-schema values via normalizeConfig.

nodes.name: resolveMode
nodes.summary: Returns the config mode, defaulting to platform-aware for null/empty/legacy configs.

nodes.name: get
nodes.summary: Dotted-path lookup of a config value; undefined when the config or the path is missing.

nodes.name: set
nodes.summary: Sets a dotted-path config value via load-mutate-write, creating the mobile-automator directory when needed and preserving other fields as pretty JSON.

nodes.name: deref
nodes.summary: Resolves a local $ref to a fixpoint with a visited-set cycle guard so self-referential or circular refs bail out instead of looping.

nodes.name: subschemaAt
nodes.summary: Walks schema properties down a dotted path, dereferencing at each hop; null for undeclared paths.

nodes.name: declaredTypesAt
nodes.summary: Returns the declared JSON types for a dotted key as an array (empty for undeclared keys).

nodes.name: collectListPaths
nodes.summary: Recursively collects every array-typed dotted path in the schema, driving read-side healing and the structural lint guard.

nodes.name: validateAt
nodes.summary: Validates a value against the subschema for a dotted key using lazily-compiled, cached Ajv validators; formats errors and strips the redundant (root) prefix.

nodes.name: emitGuide
nodes.summary: Emits raw guide markdown for a topic: ported prose loaded from the mode-specific content file and interpolated, or a minimal stub that honors the lint contracts.

nodes.name: emitSchema
nodes.summary: Reads and returns the raw JSON schema file for scenario, result, or config.

nodes.name: emitBootstrap
nodes.summary: Emits the mauto bootstrap text: the full verb map plus the locked invariants an agent needs before driving a device.

nodes.name: fallbackFor
nodes.summary: Renders the unset-placeholder fallback: empty for optional slots, otherwise "not configured — mauto config set <key>" naming the missing key.

nodes.name: firstDefined
nodes.summary: Returns the first non-empty config value among candidate keys for a placeholder, probing both flat and nested config shapes; undefined when unset.

nodes.name: renderValue
nodes.summary: Renders a resolved config value per slot spec: comma-joins arrays and applies the optional prefix.

nodes.name: interpolate
nodes.summary: Replaces every {{token}} in guide prose from config via PLACEHOLDER_KEYS, falling back per slot kind so no `{{` survives.

nodes.name: buildPromptHandlers
nodes.summary: Builds the { listPrompts, getPrompt } MCP handler pair with injectable emitGuide/config for testability; getPrompt injects mode-matched guide content as a single user message.

nodes.name: buildServer
nodes.summary: Constructs the MCP Server advertising only the prompts capability and registers listPrompts/getPrompt request handlers without connecting a transport.

nodes.name: runServer
nodes.summary: Connects the stdio transport to the built server and serves indefinitely; never called in tests because it would seize stdio.

nodes.name: scaffold
nodes.summary: Creates the mobile-automator tree, managed .gitignore, and skeleton or updated config; idempotent and returns the created paths.

nodes.name: preflightSection
nodes.summary: Extracts the preflight section of an emitted guide for artifact-reuse lint checks.

nodes.name: connection.js
nodes.summary: The single verb-facing seam for talking to a device: acquires a uniform { bridge, close } connection that transparently reuses a live session daemon or falls back to a one-shot spawn, and owns the session lifecycle ops (alive/status/spawn/shutdown).
nodes.languageNotes: CommonJS facade re-exporting daemonLogHint so cli.js reaches it through one device module.

nodes.name: acquireConnection
nodes.summary: Resolves a device connection through the daemon-vs-oneshot decision and returns a uniform { bridge, close } pair, hiding which transport backed it from the caller.

nodes.name: isSessionAlive
nodes.summary: Probes whether a device session daemon is currently reachable for the workspace by delegating to the session client's liveness check.

nodes.name: sessionStatus
nodes.summary: Reports rich daemon status (running, in-flight call count, pinned device, session id, log path), collapsing every failure branch into a not-running shape so the log path is always answerable.

nodes.name: startSession
nodes.summary: Spawns a session daemon and waits until it answers, resolving true on success.

nodes.name: endSession
nodes.summary: Asks a live daemon to shut down, resolving true when one acknowledged.

nodes.name: resolve-connection.js
nodes.summary: Decides how a one-shot verb gets its device connection — reuse a live pinned daemon, spawn-then-daemon, or one-shot fallback — via a pure strategy decision plus injected effect paths so the whole matrix is unit-testable with fakes.

nodes.name: resolveDeviceConnection
nodes.summary: Resolves the daemon-vs-oneshot strategy end to end: reuses a live daemon whose device pin matches, spawns one when autostart is on, and falls back to a one-shot mobile-mcp connection, decorating spawn failures with a daemon log hint.

nodes.name: chooseConnectionStrategy
nodes.summary: Pure decision function mapping observed facts (daemon liveness, device pin match, autostart) to daemon / oneshot / spawn-then-daemon with no collaborators or I/O.

nodes.name: deviceMatches
nodes.summary: Returns whether a daemon pinned to handleDevice satisfies a request: an unpinned request matches any live daemon, a pinned request requires equal pins.

nodes.name: readHandleDevice
nodes.summary: Projects the live daemon's pinned device out of the session handle, or null when no session exists.

nodes.name: session-client.js
nodes.summary: Client side of the device session daemon protocol over a Unix socket: multiplexes concurrent calls by id over newline-delimited JSON frames and exposes tryConnect/isAlive/requestShutdown/getSessionStatus probes.

nodes.name: connectSocket
nodes.summary: Connects a Unix socket to the daemon, resolving the connected socket or null on connection error.

nodes.name: wrapSocket
nodes.summary: Builds a { call, close, request } client over an already-connected socket, correlating pending requests by id with timeouts and failing all pending calls on socket error or close.

nodes.name: tryConnect
nodes.summary: Returns a { call, close } pair shaped exactly like a one-shot mobile-mcp connection when a live daemon is reachable, else null so the caller falls back.

nodes.name: isAlive
nodes.summary: Liveness probe: connects to the daemon and pings it, returning true only for an ok ping reply.

nodes.name: requestShutdown
nodes.summary: Sends a shutdown frame to a live daemon, resolving true when acknowledged and false when none was reachable.

nodes.name: getSessionStatus
nodes.summary: Rich status probe returning running state, in-flight call count, and pinned device, with nulls when the daemon is not running.

nodes.name: session-handle.js
nodes.summary: The single read side of mobile-automator/.session/session.json plus the CSPRNG generator for the session id it carries; total, so an absent, unreadable, or malformed handle all mean 'no session' rather than an error.

nodes.name: newSessionId
nodes.summary: Generates a 16-hex-char session id from the CSPRNG, deliberately not persisted across daemon restarts so the id changes exactly when the daemon does.

nodes.name: readHandle
nodes.summary: Reads and parses the session handle file, returning null on any absence, parse error, or non-object content.

nodes.name: readSessionId
nodes.summary: Reads the session id out of the handle and validates it against the session id pattern before returning it, else null.

nodes.name: session-log.js
nodes.summary: Owns the daemon log file lifecycle: opens a bounded append-only capture for the detached daemon's stdout/stderr, rotates it when large, and degrades to a stdio:'ignore' handle rather than failing the spawn.
nodes.languageNotes: Both stdout and stderr share one O_APPEND fd so the child's streams interleave without clobbering.

nodes.name: daemonLogHint
nodes.summary: Returns the one-sentence hint naming the daemon's captured log path so crashes stay findable.

nodes.name: openDaemonLog
nodes.summary: Opens the daemon log (creating .session/ first), rotates it if large, and returns a { stdio, write, close } handle that never degrades the spawn when the filesystem misbehaves.

nodes.name: session-paths.js
nodes.summary: Pure, side-effect-free path helpers for the per-workspace session daemon, resolving .session/ paths for the socket, pidfile, handle, log, and lock — with a hashed os.tmpdir socket fallback when the workspace path exceeds the Unix socket length limit.
nodes.languageNotes: Unix domain socket paths cap out around 104-108 bytes, so a deep project root triggers a deterministic sha1-hashed tmpdir socket.

nodes.name: sessionDir
nodes.summary: Returns the .session directory under the workspace's mobile-automator folder.

nodes.name: workspaceSocketPath
nodes.summary: Returns the canonical in-workspace Unix socket path for the session daemon.

nodes.name: socketPath
nodes.summary: Returns the socket path the daemon binds and clients connect to — the in-workspace path when short enough, else a short hashed path in the OS temp dir.

nodes.name: logFilePath
nodes.summary: Returns the workspace daemon log path, deliberately without the tmpdir fallback so the log stays next to the session it describes.

nodes.name: pidFilePath
nodes.summary: Returns the workspace pidfile path written once the daemon is listening.

nodes.name: handlePath
nodes.summary: Returns the workspace session.json handle path.

nodes.name: lockPath
nodes.summary: Returns the exclusive workspace lock path acquired before building the mobile-mcp connection so a double-spawn loser fails fast.

nodes.name: session-protocol.js
nodes.summary: Newline-delimited JSON framing for the device session daemon protocol: FrameParser encodes request/response frames and buffers partial chunks into whole parsed lines, reporting malformed lines instead of killing the connection.

nodes.name: FrameParser
nodes.summary: Owns framing on both sides of the daemon protocol: static encode() serializes a frame to one newline-terminated line, and push() buffers chunks and yields one parsed object per complete line, tolerating blank lines and reporting malformed lines as error frames.

nodes.name: session-spawn.js
nodes.summary: Spawns the device session daemon as a detached background process, wires its stdio to the workspace daemon log, and polls readiness until it answers or the timeout elapses.

nodes.name: spawnDaemon
nodes.summary: Spawns the detached daemon via an injectable child_process.spawn, records spawn-exec errors to the daemon log, unrefs the child, and polls isAlive until ready or the 15s window elapses.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to understand what mauto is: a host-agnostic CLI that turns any AI coding agent into a mobile QA engineer. It covers the 5-minute quick start (install, init, setup, device check), how the agent drives a real device through one-shot mauto verbs, the platform-aware vs. platform-agnostic modes, the full command reference, and the mobile-automator workspace layout. This document is the roadmap for everything the tour will unpack.

tour.title: CLI Entry & Dispatch
tour.description: bin/mauto.js is the process entry point: it installs an unhandledRejection safety net that routes stray async errors into the JSON envelope contract, then hands control to src/cli.js. That file is the architectural hub — with the highest fan-in (24) and fan-out (147) in the graph, it registers every mauto verb with commander and wires each handler to the device bridge, result store, memory store, and telemetry pipeline, always emitting the uniform {ok,data,error,hint,schema_version} envelope that the README's contract describes.
tour.languageLesson: Commander.js verb registration: each subcommand gets a .command()/.action() pair, and all handlers funnel through a shared envelope builder so parse failures and runtime errors produce identical JSON shapes.

tour.title: The Scenario Contract
tour.description: A mauto test is a plain JSON scenario file, and scenario_schema.json (draft-07, $schema_version 2.0/2.1) is its single source of truth: 18 step actions plus 6 precondition device actions, conditional branching, nested sub-flows, variable capture, retry policies, and 27 assertion types. The schema reference doc explains these fields and how the schema stays backwards-compatible. This is the data contract the agent authors and every later verb consumes.
tour.languageLesson: JSON Schema draft-07 with additive versioning: schema 2.1 extends 2.0 by adding a mode field and semantic actions, and a lint test enforces that newer schemas only add, never remove or reshape, existing fields.

tour.title: Workspace & Configuration
tour.description: Before any device interaction, mauto needs a mobile-automator/ workspace in the user's project. discover.js walks upward from the current directory to find it (stopping at a .git boundary), scaffold.js creates the scenarios/screenshots/results/memory tree with an idempotent setup, and config/manager.js reads and writes config.json — including the platform-aware vs. platform-agnostic mode that drives the rest of the pipeline. This is the 'setup' step of the quick start made concrete.

tour.title: Persistent Device Session Daemon
tour.description: Device interaction goes through one persistent mobile-mcp session, not per-verb spawns. session-daemon.js implements the daemon — workspace locks, framed requests over a Unix socket, idle/flush timers — while session-client.js multiplexes concurrent calls over newline-delimited JSON frames, session-paths.js resolves the .session/ socket/pidfile/log locations, and session-spawn.js launches the daemon as a detached background process. session-paths.js is the second most-depended-on module in the graph (fan-in 21), which signals how central this plumbing is.
tour.languageLesson: Unix domain socket + newline-delimited JSON framing: the daemon and client share a lightweight wire protocol where each line is one JSON request/response, with per-call ids for concurrent multiplexing — no HTTP overhead for local IPC.

tour.title: Device Bridge & Action Catalog
tour.description: The DeviceBridge facade maps every mauto device verb to a single mobile-mcp call through the session daemon, normalizing raw MCP responses into typed device, element, and crash models. action-catalog.js is the drift guard binding all 23 scenario-schema actions to their execution contracts (verb / semantic / composed / unsupported), and mobile-mcp-client.js spawns the pinned mobile-mcp server and injects the resolved device into tool calls. Building on Step 3's actions and Step 5's session, this is where a scenario step actually reaches the device.

tour.title: Platform-Agnostic Semantic Press
tour.description: In platform-agnostic mode, gestures like back, dismiss keyboard, and grant/deny permission are expressed semantically and resolved at replay time. semantic-press/index.js maps those four semantic actions to per-platform resolver methods and selects the Android or iOS strategy, hard-failing on unknown platforms. device-call.js wraps each mobile-mcp tool call with session wiring, per-call id, timeout, and observation events — the uniform telemetry that the next step's observability layer consumes.
tour.languageLesson: Strategy pattern for platform resolution: one semantic action is dispatched to a resolver object selected by platform, keeping the scenario file free of OS-specific selectors while each platform's mechanics stay encapsulated.

tour.title: Observability & Telemetry
tour.description: Device verbs must be observable without polluting stdout with logs. The observe subsystem defines a strict event shape (event.js), records it through a facade with stderr/file/spool sinks (recorder.js), gates it behind consent and a kill switch (telemetry.js), and ships batches over HTTPS with deadline-bounded POSTs (transport.js). telemetry.js has both high fan-in and high fan-out, and observe/paths.js centralizes the spool and trace file locations — observability is wired into nearly every verb.

tour.title: Reasoning & Agent Integration
tour.description: Reasoning is pulled, never ambient: the agent calls `mauto guide <topic>` on demand. guide/emitter.js is the delivery floor (fan-in 19) producing guide, schema, and bootstrap text with placeholder interpolation via guide/placeholders.js. The MCP prompts server (mcp/server.js, the graph's top code entry candidate) exposes these topics as listPrompts/getPrompt pairs, and init/adapters.js installs them as native Agent Skills per host. This is the layer that makes mauto work with any coding agent.
tour.languageLesson: Placeholder interpolation contract: guide prose carries {{token}} slots filled from config.json at emit time, with per-slot-kind fallbacks so no bare {{ survives — a lint guard enforces the invariant that emitted output never leaks a token.

tour.title: Results & Memory Persistence
tour.description: Every run produces a schema-conformant result file and feeds cross-session memory. ResultStore (result/store.js) accumulates step, assertion, crash, and observation records under an advisory lock and finalizes them, while result_schema.json defines the typed root-level observations (regression, flakiness, state_context). capability-catalog.js is the drift guard binding every result-schema fact to the mauto result verb flag that supplies it, and memory/store.js persists run-history, app-knowledge, and preferences to markdown files with atomic writes.

tour.title: Test Suite & Drift Guards
tour.description: The tests are load-bearing: unit, integration, and lint tests guard the schema, the action catalog, the capability catalog, and the guide content. tests/unit/cli.test.js exercises every mauto verb end-to-end against temp workspaces, and the tests/lint/ guards derive from the two catalogs from Steps 6 and 10 — a capability losing CLI reach fails the build. This is how the project keeps its locked invariants honest.

tour.title: CI/CD & Release Pipeline
tour.description: Merging to main triggers an automatic, fully gated release path. test.yml runs the jest suite and pack-smoke across Node 20/22/24, auto-tag.yml pushes the v<version> tag with a GitHub App token (the #170 fix — GITHUB_TOKEN pushes silently fail to trigger workflows), and release.yml resolves the tag, cuts the GitHub Release, and publishes to npm via trusted publishing (OIDC) — gated by the audit check and tests. scripts/audit-gate.js hard-fails on unaccepted high/critical production advisories. This capstone shows how the code from every prior step ships to users.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions YAML: `on` triggers select entry points, jobs run in parallel across an OS/Node matrix, and trusted publishing replaces a stored NPM_TOKEN with a workflow-level OIDC id-token — the workflow file itself is the credential.

tour.title: Architecture Documentation
tour.description: Finish with the two documents that tie the whole system together. docs/concepts/architecture.md explains the agent/mauto/mobile-mcp contract, the system components, the end-to-end generate and execute data flows, and key design decisions with a worked login-flow example. CLAUDE.md is the developer guide — architecture, drift-guard catalogs, placeholder contract, locked invariants, milestone workflow, and the release pipeline — giving a maintainer the full mental model the tour just built.
